summary: Simvastatin is a prodrug HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL-C and reduces cardiovascular events. Dosed 20-40 mg once daily in the evening; the 80 mg dose is restricted to patients already tolerating it chronically because of higher myopathy risk. Drug-interaction-driven dose caps are important.
indications: Reduce risk of total mortality, coronary heart disease death, non-fatal MI, stroke and revascularization in adults at high risk of CHD events
Primary hyperlipidemia in adults (adjunct to diet)
Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) in adults and children >=10 years
Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) as adjunct to other LDL-lowering therapy
Primary dysbetalipoproteinemia and hypertriglyceridemia (adjunct to diet)

dosage.d: 20-40 mg once daily in the evening
dosage.n: Max 40 mg/day; 80 mg only if tolerated chronically >=12 mo

dosage.d: 10-40 mg once daily in the evening
40 mg once daily in the evening

admin: Take orally once daily in the evening
May be taken with or without food
Reassess LDL-C as early as 4 weeks after start or change
moa: Simvastatin is a prodrug hydrolyzed to its active beta-hydroxyacid form (simvastatin acid), which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme converting HMG-CoA to mevalonate in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Reduced intracellular cholesterol upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, increasing LDL clearance and lowering LDL-C, total cholesterol and triglycerides.

absolute: Acute liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations
Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, voriconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, cobicistat)
relative: History of liver disease or heavy alcohol use
Risk factors for myopathy (advanced age, hypothyroidism, renal impairment, low body weight)
monitor: Concomitant amiodarone, amlodipine, verapamil, diltiazem, ranolazine

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Discontinue when pregnancy is recognized; statins may impair fetal cholesterol-dependent development and offer no benefit during pregnancy.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding due to potential for serious adverse effects in the infant. Discontinue drug or nursing.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment generally needs no adjustment. Severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): start 5 mg/day and use caution at doses above 10 mg/day.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Use caution with history of liver disease or heavy alcohol use; monitor LFTs.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, clarithromycin, erythromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, cobicistat) - contraindicated
Verapamil, diltiazem - cap simvastatin at 10 mg/day
Amiodarone, amlodipine, ranolazine - cap simvastatin at 20 mg/day
moderate: Other fibrates and niacin (>=1 g/day) - myopathy risk
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice markedly increases simvastatin levels; avoid.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; heavy use raises hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases and creatine kinase; may increase INR with warfarin.

emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine)

monitoring: Lipid panel at baseline and 4-12 weeks after start/change
Liver enzymes at baseline; repeat if clinically indicated
Creatine kinase if unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
counsel: Take once daily in the evening
Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness promptly
Tell providers about all medicines (many interactions cap your dose)
Do not use if pregnant or breastfeeding
pearls: Prodrug requiring hepatic activation, unlike atorvastatin/rosuvastatin
Dose best in the evening when cholesterol synthesis peaks
80 mg dose restricted to patients tolerating it chronically >=12 months
Many fixed dose caps with CYP3A4/myopathy-promoting drugs - memorize them
missed: Take the missed evening dose when remembered the same night; if it is nearly the next day, skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Treat symptomatically and supportively; monitor for muscle and liver effects. Highly protein-bound, so dialysis is not expected to help.
